relationships.target: Company’s new contractual requirements for third-party app developers and app marketplaces
relationships.description: Article 6 (4) Investigation relates to Apple Inc.'s new contractual requirements for third-party app developers and app marketplaces.
European Commission fined Apple Inc. €500 million in the Article 5 (4) Investigation.
European Commission issued a cease and desist order requiring Apple Inc. to remove restrictions.
The cease and desist order requires removal of technical and commercial restrictions.
Apple Inc. appealed the Commission's Article 5 (4) decision.
European Commission issued preliminary findings in the Article 6 (4) Investigation.
European Commission can issue a cease and desist order in the Article 6 (4) Investigation.
European Commission can impose fines up to 10% of Apple Inc.'s annual worldwide net sales.
European Commission may seek to impose additional fines if Apple Inc. violates a cease and desist order.
Apple Inc. believes it complies with the Digital Markets Act.
Apple Inc. has made changes to its compliance plan.

relationships.target: U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey
relationships.description: U.S. Department of Justice filed a lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey against Apple Inc.
U.S. Department of Justice filed a lawsuit against Apple Inc.
The lawsuit alleges violation of U.S. antitrust laws.
Epic Games, Inc. filed a lawsuit in the California District Court against Apple Inc.
Epic Games, Inc. filed a lawsuit against Apple Inc.
The lawsuit alleges violations of federal and state antitrust laws.
The lawsuit alleges violations of California's unfair competition law.
The lawsuit is based upon Apple Inc.'s operation of its App Store.
California District Court found that provisions of Apple's App Review Guidelines violate California's unfair competition law.
California District Court issued the 2021 Injunction to Apple Inc.

The 2021 Injunction enjoins Apple Inc. from prohibiting developers from including buttons, external links, or other calls to action that direct customers to purchasing mechanisms other than Apple's in-app purchase system.
